Description: The starting node identifier for the road segment from the OSMnx graph.
The ending node identifier for the road segment from the OSMnx graph.
The key differentiating multiple edges between the same u and v nodes.
OSM tag describing access restrictions for the road segment.
The primary OSM highway classification tag (e.g., motorway, primary, residential).
The number of traffic lanes on the road segment.
The posted speed limit for the road segment.
The official or common name of the road.
Indicates if the road segment is one-way.
The surface material of the road (e.g., asphalt, gravel).
The length of the road segment in miles.
A cleaned-up version of the road name.
The name of the intersection at the starting node (u).
The name of the intersection at the ending node (v).
Estimated travel time in seconds for the road segment based on length and speed limit.
The additional travel time (in seconds) incurred by taking a detour if this segment were closed.
Reason the segment is unusable in a flood scenario (e.g., 'FLOODED', 'BRIDGE_FUNCTIONALLY_DISCONNECTED').
The numeric FEMA risk level causing the non-functionality.
The flood frequency ('100 YEAR' or '500 YEAR') associated with the non-functionality.
The numeric FEMA risk level at which a non-flooded segment becomes isolated.
The flood frequency ('100 YEAR' or '500 YEAR') causing the isolation.
A list of unique TRANSCOM event IDs that affected this segment.
The total count of unique TRANSCOM events on this segment.
The count of distinct, continuous time periods (islands) of disruption on this segment.
Total duration in hours of all disruptive incidents, with overlapping times merged.
Count of distinct "road closed" incidents.
Total duration in hours of "road closed" incidents.
Count of distinct "road flooded" incidents.
Total duration in hours of "road flooded" incidents.
The GEOID of the Core-Based Statistical Area (CBSA) for which centrality was calculated.
The name of the CBSA.
The edge betweenness centrality score, normalized within its home CBSA.
The rank of the centrality score, normalized across all CBSAs.
Annual Average Daily Traffic from NYSDOT RIS.
Single-Unit truck Annual Average Daily Traffic from NYSDOT RIS.
Combination-Unit truck Annual Average Daily Traffic from NYSDOT RIS.
The Culvert Identification Number (CIN) if a large culvert from NYSDOT RIS is on this segment.
The total number of times the road segment intersects with a National Hydrography Dataset flowline.
Normalized redundancy score (0-10 scale). A higher score indicates lower redundancy (worse).
Binned redundancy score (1-5). A higher score indicates lower redundancy (worse).
Calculated flood risk score based on FEMA data (100-year=2, 500-year=1).
Calculated risk score from historical TRANSCOM flooding events (1 event=1, >1 event=2).
The normalized network centrality score, indicating structural importance.
Binary risk score indicating the presence of a large culvert (0 or 1).
Binary risk score indicating an intersection with a water flowline (0 or 1).
Composite score combining centrality and redundancy. Higher score indicates higher criticality.
Alternate composite criticality score using binned redundancy weight.
Composite score summing multiple hazard risk factors (flood, culvert, hydrography, events).
Final inverse resilience score. A higher score indicates a segment is highly critical AND at high risk.
Alternate final inverse resilience score using binned criticality.
The geometry of the road segment.
